rows.name: world_number (first digit of the HUD WORLD display)
rows.notes: Encoding: one byte, 0-based (0 = World 1). The HUD/card prints value+1 as the first digit of WORLD. In World 1-1 this byte reads 0 (aligned with $075C=0 while the HUD showed WORLD 1-1). Found with no reference: the value does not change by playing, so the neighborhood was narrowed from the known lives counter $075A (read 1 after one intentional death) and the candidate proven by write. Proof by write: paused mid-level, wrote $075F=6 alone (leaving $075C=4, the level byte) and lost a life; after the level reloaded the HUD read WORLD 7-5 (screenshot) - only the world digit moved 1 -> 7, so $075F is the world byte. A combined earlier test (wrote $075F=4 and $075C=2) produced WORLD 5-3. Source: differential search.

rows.name: level_number (second digit of the HUD WORLD display)
rows.notes: Encoding: one byte, 0-based (0 = 1st level, e.g. 1-1; 4 = 5th level). The HUD/card prints value+1 as the second digit of WORLD. In World 1-1 this byte reads 0 (aligned with $075F=0 while the HUD showed WORLD 1-1). Found with no reference: value does not change by playing, so the neighborhood was narrowed from the known lives counter $075A and proven by write. Proof by write: restored to 1-1, wrote $075C=4 alone (leaving $075F=0, the world byte) and lost a life; after reload the HUD read WORLD 1-5 (screenshot) - only the level digit moved 1 -> 5. A combined test (wrote $075F=4 and $075C=2) produced WORLD 5-3. Source: differential search.
